status: draft-v4 (internal assistive; a human reviewer is the final authority)

defaults.perspective_preference: Mutual reciprocal mNDA: both Parties may disclose and receive, terms protect Amperesand symmetrically as both Disclosing and Receiving Party. With an individual counterparty (the template Purpose is exploring a potential employment relationship), Amperesand is in practice the primary discloser of business/IP/product information and the individual is the primary recipient, but the agreement remains drafted mutually so an individual who shares personal know-how or materials is also protected.
defaults.forum: AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules, single arbitrator, seat Nevada USA, English; injunctive/equitable-relief court carve-out (any court of competent jurisdiction)
defaults.term_standard: Agreement term 1 year from the Effective Date, terminable earlier by either Party on written notice (template Clause 8).
defaults.survival_standard: Confidentiality obligations survive 2 years from the Effective Date; trade secrets protected for as long as they remain trade secrets under DTSA / applicable state UTSA (template Clause 8). This is a MUTUAL NDA, so the unilateral-NDA per-disclosure survival default does NOT apply here (that default is for UNILATERAL Individual paper); the mutual 2-year-from-Effective-Date + perpetual-trade-secret standard governs, consistent with the mutual US-company variant. Counsel may consider re-anchoring survival to termination/expiry to lengthen the tail on short-term agreements.
required_carveouts: prior_possession (already in the Receiving Party's or its Representatives' possession/known before disclosure)
public_domain (is or comes into the public domain through no fault or breach by the Receiving Party or its Representatives)
third_party (received from a third party not known to be under any confidentiality obligation)
independent_development (independently developed without regard or reference to the Confidential Information)
written_authorization (approved for release or use by written authorization of the Disclosing Party)
counsel_must_confirm: This variant is derived by transfer from the mutual US-company variant plus the canonical template, with no executed examples of this exact variant sampled. Confidence is medium; counsel should validate the individual-counterparty adjustments before relying on them.

Clean the template party block for a US individual: the canonical template identifies the Counterparty by 'Singapore NRIC/Passport number' and the Purpose as 'explore a potential employment relationship' -- for a US natural person use the appropriate US identifier (and only last four digits) and confirm/replace the Purpose; do not leave Singapore-specific identifiers in a Delaware-governed US individual agreement.

Confirm the perpetual/uncapped trade-secret tail is the approved standard default where an individual's house form (rare) or a recruiter/agency intermediary proposes a flat survival period with no trade-secret carve-out.

Individual-enforceability realism: confirm the remedies posture against a natural person (injunctive relief acknowledged; indemnity and one-sided fee-shifting against an individual are dealbreaker-class and unusual to encounter, but flag if a counterparty intermediary inserts them).

Confirm the personal_data_privacy position scope for a US individual: the individual's personal data is handled under US privacy norms (no PDPA -- PDPA applies only to the SG variant); confirm whether any state-specific privacy obligations (e.g., CCPA where the individual is a California resident and Amperesand processes their data) need to be acknowledged.

Per-deal judgment on the governing-law/forum fallback ladder where an individual is represented by counsel or routed through an agency/recruiter house form that proposes a different US state's law or court litigation in lieu of AAA arbitration.

positions.title: Definition of Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: Confidential Information is defined broadly (template Clause 1) as any and all information relating to the Purpose, disclosed or communicated by or on behalf of a Party (Disclosing Party) that is marked or communicated as confidential, expressly including: (a) business/affairs/customers/suppliers/plans/market-opportunity info and IP/operations/processes/product/know-how/technical/designs/trade-secrets/software of the Disclosing Party and its existing or future subsidiaries; (b) information/findings/data/analysis derived from the CI; (c) shared personal data; and (d) any other info identified as confidential at disclosure, including third-party confidential info held by the Disclosing Party. A reasonable-person catch-all sweeps in unmarked information that someone familiar with the subject area would recognize as the type typically treated as confidential, or that the Receiving Party has reason to believe may be confidential. No oral-to-writing confirmation deadline and no marking requirement to qualify. (Note: the Disclosing-Party subsidiary/group language operates in Amperesand's favor as discloser; an individual counterparty has no subsidiaries, so that branch is one-sided toward Amperesand by design and is acceptable.)
walk_away_triggers: Definition narrowed to require written marking (or a stamp/legend) before disclosure to qualify, with oral/visual disclosures protected only if reduced to writing and marked within a fixed deadline -- loses protection for Amperesand's own unmarked oral disclosures to the individual (especially likely in an in-person interview/employment-exploration context where most disclosure is oral).

Burden-of-proof-on-Receiving-Party language paired with an unbounded 'by its nature would reasonably be construed as Confidential' catch-all that gives Amperesand no marking safe harbor when Amperesand is the recipient.

Definition hard-scoped to a single technology or category such that Amperesand's broader shared information (financials, strategy, personnel, customers) falls outside protection -- treat as walk-away when Amperesand is the primary discloser of IP.

Runaway scope beyond the Purpose or beyond formal disclosure ('whether or not related to the project'; 'in the ordinary course of conducting business'; constructive/inferred/observed knowledge catch-alls) -- creates inadvertent-breach exposure for the individual (and for Amperesand where Amperesand is the recipient).

Singapore PDPA / Companies Act / Electronic Transactions Act statutory references embedded in a Delaware-governed US agreement, creating ambiguity over the governing privacy regime -- must be cleaned before signing (the canonical template carries Singapore-identifier artifacts that must be replaced for a US individual).
Cloud/third-party-processing acknowledgment in the definition that can be read as Amperesand accepting reduced confidentiality controls for cloud-stored CI.
acceptable_fallbacks: A marking/identification mechanic IS acceptable where the catch-all for reasonably-apparent-confidential information is retained, so unmarked sensitive info disclosed to the individual is still protected.
A short oral-disclosure memorialization window (>=30 days) is tolerable only if failure to memorialize does NOT strip protection from information that is confidential by its nature.
Narrowing the 'subsidiaries/group' branch is acceptable for the individual's side (the individual has none), provided Amperesand's group-disclosure scope is preserved.

positions.title: Permitted Purpose
positions.standard_position: Confidential Information may be used solely for a single, narrowly defined Purpose stated in the recitals -- for this individual mutual template, exploring a potential employment (or comparable engagement) relationship between the Parties -- and for no other purpose. The Purpose placeholder must be filled in with the specific subject matter before signature; do not leave the bracketed '[explore a potential employment relationship between the Parties]' as a placeholder if the actual purpose differs.
walk_away_triggers: Purpose that extends beyond evaluation to ongoing 'business activities that arise from the relationship' once a relationship exists, permitting open-ended use of CI without a separate employment/engagement agreement -- limit to evaluation only.

Disclosing-party-controlled open-ended catch-all ('and/or other purposes as allowed by the disclosing party') giving the individual (or their intermediary) unilateral control to expand permitted use of Amperesand's information -- strike.

Anti-reverse-engineering or 'design-around' prohibition embedded in the purpose/use clause broad enough to constrain the individual's legitimate independent skills/work, or Amperesand's legitimate independent engineering on overlapping subject matter -- narrow to genuine misappropriation of disclosed CI.

Executed agreement left with unresolved bracketed alternative Purpose language or an unfilled placeholder, creating ambiguity over agreed scope -- do not sign until the Purpose is finalized to a single complete definition.

A Purpose drafted to let the individual carry Amperesand's CI into a subsequent role with a third-party employer or to 'use general learnings in future engagements' -- strike; this is residuals-by-another-name (see residuals).
acceptable_fallbacks: A somewhat broader but still bounded Purpose (e.g., 'exploring a potential employment, consulting, or advisory relationship between the Parties') is acceptable provided it remains evaluation-oriented and not open-ended operational use.
A carve-out deferring info governed by a separate definitive employment/consulting agreement is acceptable if it does not leave pre-contract disclosures unprotected.

positions.title: Exclusions from Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: Five exclusions (template Clause 2): (a) prior possession/knowledge by the Receiving Party or its Representatives; (b) public domain through no fault/breach; (c) third-party receipt with no known confidentiality duty; (d) independent development without regard or reference to the CI; (e) approved for release by written authorization of the Disclosing Party. Compelled disclosure is handled separately as Required Disclosure (Clause 3), NOT as a sixth exclusion.
walk_away_triggers: Prior-possession / prior-knowledge carve-out entirely absent, so the individual (or Amperesand as recipient) could be bound on information it already held before disclosure -- for an individual this also matters for general skills/knowledge the person already possessed.

Independent-development carve-out absent or narrowed, exposing Amperesand to confidentiality/IP entanglement on its own R&D that overlaps the counterparty's CI, and exposing the individual on their own pre-existing know-how.
Severely truncated carve-out set (only two or three carve-outs), particularly where prior possession AND independent development are both missing.

Subjective or distorted carve-out tests that defeat legitimate exclusions -- e.g., third-party receipt conditioned on 'no knowledge of improper action by the transferor', or a regulatory carve-out so narrow it omits subpoenas/court orders.

Public-domain carve-out drafted as 'through Receiving Party breach only' that fails to cover information already public at the time of disclosure, or otherwise narrower than 'no fault of the Receiving Party'.
No compelled-disclosure mechanism at all, or one without prior-notice/minimization, leaving the individual (or Amperesand) unable to comply with a court/regulatory order without breaching.
acceptable_fallbacks: Four-exclusion sets are tolerable ONLY where both prior possession and independent development are present; if prior possession is the missing one, require it be reinstated.
A 'no wrongful act or breach by the receiving Party' public-domain formulation is acceptable (equivalent to 'no fault').
Burden of proof on the receiving party for a SPECIFIC contested exclusion is tolerable; a blanket burden-shift on all exclusions should be resisted or made mutual.

positions.title: Required (Compelled) Disclosure
positions.standard_position: Where the Receiving Party (or a Representative) is obligated or requested to disclose CI under a valid court order or governmental/regulatory authority with jurisdiction, it shall (i) to the extent not legally prohibited, give the Disclosing Party reasonable prior written notice; (ii) disclose only the CI required by the order; and (iii) use reasonable efforts to secure confidential treatment. If advance notice is impossible, inform the Disclosing Party of the full circumstances as soon as reasonably practicable after disclosure. Mutual/symmetrical. (Template Clause 3.)
walk_away_triggers: Cost of resisting/limiting compelled disclosure shifted onto Amperesand as Disclosing Party as a baseline term, or onto the individual in a way a natural person could not realistically bear.
Fixed long advance-notice periods (e.g., 30 days) that cannot be met under urgent court/government orders.

Mandatory obligation to take 'all assistance / all steps the Disclosing Party may require' to fight compelled disclosure, effectively ceding control of a party's response to legal process to the other.
No prior-notice or minimization mechanism at all, forcing the individual (or Amperesand) to choose between breaching the order and breaching the NDA.
Compelled-disclosure right made one-sided (only one party may comply with legal process; or only one party controls the response).
acceptable_fallbacks: Reasonable cooperation with the disclosing Party's efforts to seek a protective order, at the disclosing Party's expense, is acceptable.
A protective-order / 'reliable assurances of confidential treatment' framing is acceptable in place of the template's 'reasonable efforts to ensure confidential treatment'.

positions.title: Confidentiality Obligations
positions.standard_position: The Receiving Party must hold all CI in strict confidence and not disclose it to any third party without prior written approval, use it solely for the Purpose, apply at least the same degree of care it uses for its own CI of like importance but no less than reasonable care, limit access to Representatives strictly on a need-to-know basis, remain fully responsible for its Representatives' breaches and take all reasonable measures to restrain them, and promptly notify the Disclosing Party of any loss or unauthorized disclosure -- mutual, with no extraneous IP/use restrictions, marking-confirmation traps, or expanded-disclosee carve-outs. (Template Clause 4.) For an INDIVIDUAL counterparty, 'Representatives' must be read narrowly: a natural person has no directors/officers/employees, so the individual's permitted Representatives are limited to their own personal advisers (e.g., legal counsel, accountant/tax adviser) on a strict need-to-know basis -- not an open class of employees, affiliates, or agents.
walk_away_triggers: Representatives defined for the individual to include an open-ended class (employees, affiliates, agents, a future employer, recruiters, or 'any person the Counterparty deems appropriate') beyond the individual's own need-to-know personal advisers -- narrow to personal counsel/accountant on a need-to-know basis with the individual remaining fully responsible.
No-copy / no-reverse-engineer restriction drafted broadly enough to bind a party's INDEPENDENT development or pre-existing knowledge, with no independent-development carve-in -- resist or carve out.
Requirement of prior written notice to the counterparty BEFORE the Receiving Party may share with its own need-to-know advisers -- operationally unworkable.

Mandatory affirmative enforcement obligation requiring the Receiving Party to take 'all reasonable measures including court proceedings' against its own Representatives at its own cost -- push back, as it is unrealistic to impose mandated litigation on a natural person.
Requirement that each Representative individually execute identical written undertakings before any access, framed as an unworkable precondition -- resist.

Strict 'best endeavours to prevent breach' or 'whichever is higher / generally-accepted-standards' care obligation imposing costly affirmative steps beyond reasonable care -- especially unreasonable to impose on a natural person.
AI-training / AI-tool-development prohibition or one-sided cybersecurity-audit/remediation regime bolted onto the confidentiality clause.
Perpetual or open-ended confidentiality obligation embedded in this clause (including 'indefinite' obligations) that contradicts the agreed term.

Broad 'no use/exploitation for any commercial purpose whatsoever without written approval' restriction that exceeds the Purpose limitation and could constrain the individual's ordinary professional livelihood -- narrow to use of disclosed CI only.
acceptable_fallbacks: Reverse-engineering prohibitions are acceptable when expressly carved to permit independent development and exclude information covered by the exclusions.
A use-restriction to 'the purposes of this Agreement' is acceptable and mirrors the template Purpose limitation.

For an individual, requiring the few personal advisers who receive CI to be informed of and bound by equivalent confidentiality obligations (with the individual responsible for their compliance) is acceptable in lieu of a formal Representative-flowdown.

'Need to know' Representative scope for the individual may include the individual's legal/financial advisers and, where genuinely necessary for the Purpose, a named immediate adviser, provided the responsibility-for-breach backstop is retained.
An affirmative enforcement obligation against the Receiving Party's own Representatives is acceptable only as responsibility for Representatives' breaches, not mandated litigation.
A requirement that each Representative individually execute identical written undertakings before any access is acceptable in principle for an individual's small adviser set.

positions.title: Permitted Disclosures (Representatives and Compelled)
positions.standard_position: The Receiving Party may disclose CI (a) to its Representatives on a need-to-know basis for the Purpose, remaining responsible for their compliance -- for the individual, limited to the person's own need-to-know personal advisers (legal/financial) -- and (b) where compelled by a valid court/governmental/regulatory order, subject to the Required Disclosure protections (notice, minimization, confidential-treatment efforts). All disclosure rights mutual/symmetrical. The template's 'No Publicity' clause (Clause 5) is the standard and acceptable: the individual may not make any public release or announcement about the Purpose without Amperesand's written approval.
walk_away_triggers: Disclosure to open-ended classes of third parties (a future/prospective employer, recruiters, an agency network, 'any party the Counterparty wishes to consult') -- broad leakage of Amperesand CI to unidentified parties without consent.
Requiring prior written notice to the counterparty before the Receiving Party may share with its OWN need-to-know advisers -- operationally unworkable.

Unilateral government/regulator pass-through letting only one party disclose the other's CI to a government agency without notice or reciprocity, or a standing third-party inspection right not tied to actual legal compulsion.

Expansion of the 'No Publicity' clause into a broad gag barring even the individual's truthful description of their own role/skills, or barring acknowledgment of the existence of discussions in a way that interferes with the individual's ordinary job search -- resist expansions beyond non-disclosure of CI.
Mandatory obligation to take 'all steps the Disclosing Party may require' to fight compelled disclosure where this cedes control of a party's legal response to the other.
acceptable_fallbacks: Disclosure to the individual's personal legal/financial advisers with a need to know, under confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than the NDA, is acceptable provided it is reciprocal and the individual remains responsible.
The template 'No Publicity' restriction (Clause 5) limited to the Purpose and matters contemplated by the Agreement is acceptable.

positions.title: Term and Survival of Confidentiality
positions.standard_position: Agreement term commences on the Effective Date and expires 1 year from the Effective Date, terminable earlier by either Party on written notice. Confidentiality obligations survive any termination/expiration for 2 years from the Effective Date; trade secrets remain Confidential Information for as long as they so qualify under DTSA / applicable state UTSA. (Template Clause 8.) This is a MUTUAL NDA, so the survival standard is the mutual 2-year-from-Effective-Date + perpetual-trade-secret rule (NOT the unilateral-Individual per-disclosure default, which applies only to unilateral-NDA Individual paper).
walk_away_triggers: No post-termination survival at all, or confidentiality co-terminous with the agreement term, leaving disclosed info unprotected once the (short) term ends.
Survival measured from the Effective Date where the survival figure equals or is shorter than the agreement term, producing zero or near-zero effective post-expiry protection.
Flat survival period with NO trade-secret carve-out where Amperesand is the sole/primary discloser -- insist on at minimum a trade-secret carve-out.

Perpetual or indefinite survival imposed on the individual (or on Amperesand as recipient) for ordinary CI -- a perpetual confidentiality obligation on a natural person is both unreasonable and of doubtful enforceability; cap ordinary-CI survival to a finite period and reserve perpetuity for genuine trade secrets only.
Internally contradictory or ambiguous survival drafting a court could read as either expiring with the agreement or perpetual -- fix to a clear finite period before signing.
Drafting-error figures (a spelled-out number disagreeing with its parenthetical figure) creating construction-dispute risk -- correct before execution.

Term of 5 years or longer, or a perpetual/evergreen term with no fixed expiry surviving indefinitely absent affirmative notice, especially where the early-termination-for-convenience right is also removed.
acceptable_fallbacks: 3-year survival measured from each disclosure is an acceptable fallback IF a perpetual trade-secret carve-out is added.
Re-anchoring survival to termination/expiry (rather than the Effective Date) is a welcome forward-looking improvement that lengthens the post-expiry tail.
A 2-year-from-Effective-Date survival on a 1-year term (the template form) is the standard and acceptable, with the trade-secret tail providing long-term protection for genuine trade secrets.

positions.title: Survival of Obligations
positions.standard_position: Each Party's rights and obligations survive termination/expiration of the Agreement for the confidentiality-survival period (2 years from the Effective Date) with trade secrets surviving for as long as they remain trade secrets; surviving obligations (and the duty to protect any lawfully retained copy) continue independently of the agreement term. (Template Clauses 7-8.)
walk_away_triggers: Survival of obligations tied solely to the agreement term so that nothing survives expiry/termination.
Perpetual/indefinite survival of ALL obligations imposed on the individual (distinct from the legitimate perpetual trade-secret tail) -- unreasonable against a natural person.
Survival clause that revives or extends restraints (non-solicit/non-compete-style obligations) beyond confidentiality.
Ambiguous interplay between the survival clause and the retained-copy carve-out that could be read as perpetual confidentiality on all retained data.
acceptable_fallbacks: Survival expressly limited to confidentiality, return/destruction, no-license, and remedies provisions is acceptable.

Survival of the duty to protect a single lawfully retained archival copy for as long as retained is acceptable (and, for an individual who is unlikely to maintain formal backup systems, a simple destruction certification is usually preferable to a retained-copy carve-out).

positions.title: Return or Destruction of Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: On the Disclosing Party's written request or upon expiration/termination, the Receiving Party must within 14 days return or destroy (at its election) all CI and copies, except it may retain one (1) archival copy (including electronic records created by automatic archiving/back-up) solely to perform surviving obligations and as required by law/court/regulatory authority or internal audit/compliance, with the Agreement continuing to apply to any retained copy. (Template Clause 7.) For an individual, return/destruction is typically simpler -- a destruction certification covering documents, emails, and devices on which Amperesand CI was stored is the practical standard.
walk_away_triggers: Destroy/return obligation satisfied merely by reference to the Receiving Party's own record-retention schedule, letting the counterparty keep Amperesand CI as long as its policies permit -- renders the destroy obligation illusory.
Open-ended/indefinite retention of automatic backup or archival copies with no sunset and a perpetual confidentiality tail.

Broad carve-out permitting retention of derivative work product (notes, summaries, analyses) so materials derived from Amperesand CI need not be returned or destroyed -- particularly relevant for an individual's interview/evaluation notes.
Loss of any trigger for return on demand (obligation arises only on a 'decision not to proceed' with no right for Amperesand to demand return at any time or on expiry).
Return-only obligation with no destruction option and no certification mechanism (impractical for a natural person's personal files/devices).
acceptable_fallbacks: A 14-day window on written notice matching the template is acceptable.
A written destruction certification in lieu of physical return is acceptable and preferred, especially for an individual's personal devices and electronically stored CI.

Retention of a single archival copy strictly to perform surviving obligations and as required by law is acceptable; for an individual, a clean destruction is usually preferable to any retained-copy carve-out.

positions.title: No License / No Transfer of IP
positions.standard_position: The Disclosing Party retains all right, title, and interest in its CI (including copies and extracts) and grants no licenses or rights except as expressly set forth; nothing grants any license to, or waives, any patents, copyrights, trademarks, or mask works (express, implied, by estoppel, or otherwise). (Template Clause 10.)
walk_away_triggers: Any IP assignment, vesting, or work-for-hire obligation requiring Amperesand (as recipient) to assign or transfer ownership of IP, inventions, or 'derivatives of Confidential Information' it creates -- strike or carve out Amperesand's pre-existing and independently developed IP. (Note: an NDA is not the place to assign the individual's inventions either; genuine invention-assignment belongs in a separate employment/consulting agreement.)
A patent-filing prohibition barring a party from filing patent applications relating to information it receives -- resist or narrow.

'Derived directly or indirectly' or 'in the course of interaction' IP-capture language sweeping in a party's own innovations that merely touch the other's information -- require a carve-out for pre-existing, independently developed, and (for the individual) general-skill/residual-knowledge IP.
Any provision granting the Receiving Party an affirmative license to the Disclosing Party's IP, or deeming disclosure an implied license/waiver of patent/copyright/trademark/mask-work rights.
acceptable_fallbacks: A 'no license under any trade secrets, copyrights, know-how, or other rights granted or implied' formulation is acceptable and mirrors the template.
If the individual will create work product during the engagement, defer invention-assignment to a separate employment/consulting agreement rather than burying it in the NDA.

positions.title: No Warranty / AS-IS
positions.standard_position: Confidential Information is provided AS IS with the Disclosing Party making no representation or warranty (express, statutory, or implied) as to accuracy, completeness, fitness, or performance, and bearing no liability for the Receiving Party's use or reliance; the Disclosing Party is under no obligation to supply any particular CI and neither Party is obligated to enter into any transaction (no partnership/JV/agency/employment created). (Template Clause 6 'No Other Obligations'; the no-obligation-to-deal function is template-true. An explicit AS-IS warranty disclaimer is common to add and acceptable when mutual.)
walk_away_triggers: A consequential/indirect/special/punitive damages waiver or any liability cap bundled into the no-warranty clause that would limit Amperesand's recovery when the individual misuses or improperly discloses Amperesand's CI -- if it must remain, carve out confidentiality breaches and IP misappropriation from the waiver.
Outright deletion of any AS-IS disclaimer, leaving Amperesand exposed to accuracy/completeness/quality claims about the information it shares.
A one-directional damages exclusion or non-reliance limitation protecting only the counterparty as discloser while leaving Amperesand fully liable -- require mutuality.
Any affirmative warranty by Amperesand beyond a narrow right-to-disclose (warranting accuracy, completeness, non-infringement, fitness, or performance of Amperesand's CI) -- refuse.
A no-warranty clause coupled with an indemnity on Amperesand for the individual's use of or reliance on the disclosed information -- refuse (indemnity in an NDA is dealbreaker-class).
acceptable_fallbacks: A mutual AS-IS / no-warranty disclaimer is acceptable and preferred.
The template Clause 6 'No Other Obligations' (no compulsion to supply information; no compulsion to enter any transaction) is the standard and is template-true.

positions.title: Remedies / Injunctive Relief
positions.standard_position: Each Party acknowledges monetary damages alone may be insufficient and agrees the Disclosing Party (either Party in this mutual NDA) may seek specific performance or injunctive relief from any court in any jurisdiction, as a non-exclusive remedy in addition to all other remedies at law or in equity, with no waiver or cap on monetary damages. (Template Clause 12.)
walk_away_triggers: Recipient must waive all rights to oppose the granting of injunctive/equitable relief (a blanket pre-emptive waiver of a party's defense rights) -- refuse; particularly inappropriate to extract from an individual.
A low or fixed bond cap (a nominal dollar ceiling) that a court could read as limiting the relief or security available -- refuse any numeric bond cap.
Prevailing-party attorneys'-fee shifting tied to remedies/enforcement -- resist; against a natural person, one-sided fee-shifting is coercive and a dealbreaker.
Liquidated-damages or penalty provision specifying a fixed sum payable by the individual on breach -- refuse (likely an unenforceable penalty and disproportionate against a natural person).
Injunctive relief narrowed to IP-rights infringement only, excluding ordinary confidentiality breaches.
Complete omission of any injunctive-relief/irreparable-harm clause, leaving Amperesand without express equitable-remedy acknowledgment.
Injunctive/no-oppose right made one-sided in the counterparty's favour, or against Amperesand, in a mutual NDA.
Indemnification or uncapped damages liability bundled into the remedies clause beyond standard NDA scope.
acceptable_fallbacks: A 'no necessity of posting a bond' formulation is acceptable and favorable.
Equitable relief framed as available to the 'non-breaching Party' is acceptable as a mutual formulation.
Limiting injunctive relief to 'a court of competent jurisdiction' (rather than 'any court in any jurisdiction') is acceptable provided the arbitration carve-out for injunctive relief is preserved.

positions.title: Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
positions.standard_position: Governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. Disputes referred to arbitration by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, single arbitrator, seat Nevada USA, conducted in English, with a court carve-out permitting either Party to seek injunctive/equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction. Trade-secret basis is DTSA / applicable state UTSA. (Template Clause 16.)
walk_away_triggers: No governing law and no dispute-resolution/forum clause at all (uncertain applicable law and enforcement).
Governing law specified but NO forum or dispute mechanism (insist on a clear court or arbitration forum).

Litigation in the individual's (or their intermediary's) home courts of an adverse jurisdiction with exclusive jurisdiction and consent to personal jurisdiction -- refuse a one-sided home-forum lock; counter to Delaware law + AAA Nevada, or a neutral US state.
Wholly foreign, non-US legal regime with foreign-seat litigation/arbitration giving the counterparty home-court advantage.

Mixed/inconsistent templates: a Delaware-governed contract embedding operative Singapore statutory definitions (personal-data, companies-act, electronic-transactions statutes) with no conflicts carve-out -- the canonical template carries Singapore-identifier artifacts (NRIC/Passport) that must be cleaned for a US individual.
Ambiguous choice-of-law language such as 'internal laws of the United States' -- require a named state's law (Delaware).
Internally contradictory or unenforceable forum clause naming two incompatible institutions or seats in one provision.
ICC arbitration for a low-value NDA dispute (disproportionate cost) where AAA or SIAC was available -- doubly disproportionate against an individual.
acceptable_fallbacks: Delaware law with AAA arbitration seated in a US state other than Nevada is an acceptable fallback though Nevada is the template standard.
A neutral US state's substantive law is acceptable per-deal where the counterparty's intermediary form requires it and the forum remains a neutral US arbitral seat or court.

US court litigation in a neutral or Delaware venue is an acceptable fallback in lieu of AAA arbitration where an individual reasonably objects to arbitration cost, subject to counsel sign-off and resisting the counterparty's exclusive home venue.

positions.title: Assignment
positions.standard_position: Neither Party may assign rights or delegate obligations without the other Party's prior written consent, except (i) the Disclosing Party may assign to an acquirer of substantially all its assets directly or by operation of law, and (ii) Amperesand (Party A) may assign to any Affiliate on prior written notice only (no consent required). Any purported assignment in violation is null and void; assignment does not relieve the assignor of its obligations; the Agreement is for the sole benefit of the Parties and their successors and permitted assigns (no third-party beneficiaries). (Template Clause 15.) An individual counterparty has no affiliates, so the Affiliate-assignment carve-out runs one way to Amperesand by design and is acceptable.
walk_away_triggers: Agreement freely binding on 'successors and assigns' with no consent or notice requirement, allowing either party to assign automatically and transfer access to Amperesand's CI to an unknown third party.
An individual purporting to be able to assign the agreement (and access to Amperesand's CI) to a future employer or other third party without consent.
In a mutual NDA, the assignment restriction framed only against the 'Recipient', leaving the Discloser free to assign without consent.
M&A/change-of-control carve-out with a one-sided non-competitor restriction applying only to Amperesand's acquirer.
No assignment clause at all, leaving assignment to permissive local-law defaults.
acceptable_fallbacks: A flat mutual 'no assignment without prior written consent' is acceptable when symmetrical, even if it drops Amperesand's Affiliate-on-notice carve-out.
Amperesand's Affiliate-assignment-on-notice right (template Clause 15) is the preferred position and is acceptable as drafted (the individual has no equivalent need).

positions.title: Residuals (Prohibited)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's template contains NO residuals clause and no competitive-use carve-out; the recipient must keep CI confidential and use it solely for the Purpose, with no right to use memory-retained 'residuals'. For an individual, this is acute: a residuals clause would in effect let the person carry Amperesand's CI into a future role. The recipient may continue to use their own general skills, experience, and unaided general knowledge (which are NOT Amperesand CI), but may not use or disclose Amperesand's specific Confidential Information.
walk_away_triggers: Broad residuals clause permitting the individual to use information retained in unaided memory for any purpose, including a subsequent role with another employer.
Competitive-use carve-out expressly permitting the individual to use Amperesand's CI to evaluate, join, or build a competing product or company.
Any residuals or 'general learnings' clause lacking an express prohibition on direct use of Confidential Information.
A clause purporting to convert Amperesand's specific CI into the individual's freely usable 'experience' or 'skill'.
acceptable_fallbacks: An acknowledgment that the individual remains free to use their own pre-existing general skills, experience, and unaided general knowledge (expressly excluding any use or disclosure of Amperesand's specific Confidential Information and excluding deliberate memorization) is acceptable and appropriate for a natural person; full residuals language is not.

positions.title: Non-Solicitation (Prohibited)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's template contains NO standalone non-solicitation covenant; an NDA is a confidentiality instrument, not a trade-restraint vehicle. An inserted non-solicit is a prohibited, high-severity, walk-away clause. (Genuine post-employment non-solicit covenants, if any, belong in a separate employment/consulting agreement subject to applicable state restraint-of-trade law, not in this NDA.)
walk_away_triggers: Any standalone non-solicitation covenant untethered from use of Confidential Information inserted into the NDA.
Non-solicit period exceeding 12 months, or with no fixed term / perpetual restraint.
Unilateral / one-way non-solicit binding only the individual (or only Amperesand).
Non-solicit lacking a general-advertising and non-targeted-recruiting carve-out.
Customer/supplier non-solicit broad enough to restrain the individual's ordinary livelihood (a de facto non-compete).
Any accompanying non-competition covenant.
Liquidated-damages or indemnity tied to a non-solicit breach.
acceptable_fallbacks: No fallback as an NDA term; any genuine non-solicit is escalated to counsel for a separate employment/consulting agreement subject to state restraint-of-trade enforceability, not accepted in the NDA.

positions.title: Non-Competition (Prohibited)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's NDA template contains NO non-competition clause; the NDA remains a confidentiality instrument only. Preferred position is no non-compete in either direction. (Any genuine non-compete with an individual belongs in a separate agreement subject to state enforceability law -- non-competes against natural persons are void or heavily restricted in a growing number of US states.)
walk_away_triggers: Any non-compete restraint on the individual embedded in the NDA, barring the person from working for a competitor or in a field of work.
A non-compete-taint / 'residual contamination' restriction barring the individual (or Amperesand personnel) exposed to CI from working on competing technology -- a de facto non-compete.
Broad definition of 'competes' (same/similar functionality) tied to a personnel-segregation or taint obligation.
Any asymmetric non-compete binding only one party in a mutual NDA.
A non-compete waiver extracted from Amperesand with no reciprocal protection.
acceptable_fallbacks: No fallback as an NDA term; deletion is the only standard position. Any genuine non-compete is escalated to counsel for a separate agreement subject to state enforceability law (many US states void non-competes against natural persons).

positions.title: Indemnification (Prohibited)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's standard NDA contains NO indemnification, hold-harmless, or fee-shifting provision; confidentiality breaches are remedied through general-law damages and equitable relief. Preferred position is to strike any indemnity or attorneys'-fees clause entirely. An uncapped indemnity against a natural person is especially inappropriate and coercive.
walk_away_triggers: Any indemnity running against the individual for breach -- dealbreaker-class; an individual cannot realistically bear an uncapped indemnity and it is coercive.
Legal/attorneys' costs recoverable on a solicitor-client or 'indemnity basis' rather than reasonable party-and-party costs.
Indemnity or liability extending to 'attempted or threatened' disclosure/violation.
Uncapped explicit damages liability for unauthorized use/disclosure with no limitation of liability.
Any non-mutual fee-shifting or indemnity that runs only in one party's favour.
A fixed liquidated-damages sum payable by the individual on breach (likely an unenforceable penalty).
acceptable_fallbacks: No standard fallback; strike. If a counterparty intermediary insists on any liability allocation, escalate to counsel -- the only entertained form would be mutual, capped, and confidentiality-breach-only, excluding indirect/consequential loss.

positions.title: Personal Data / Privacy (Individual)
positions.standard_position: Where the individual's own personal data is exchanged or processed in connection with the Purpose (e.g., the person's identifiers, contact details, or background information shared during employment exploration), it is treated as Confidential Information (the template definition expressly includes 'any shared personal data') and is handled under applicable US privacy norms. This is the US variant, so PDPA does NOT apply (PDPA is the SG-variant standard); the personal-data handling baseline is US federal/state law, with no foreign statutory regime imported. Personal data is used solely for the Purpose, protected with at least reasonable care, and returned/destroyed with other CI.
walk_away_triggers: Singapore PDPA (or Companies Act / Electronic Transactions Act) obligations imported into this Delaware-governed US individual agreement -- the canonical template carries Singapore-identifier artifacts (NRIC/Passport); strike the SG regime and use US identifiers/norms.

A standalone data-privacy / data-breach regime imposing fixed breach-notification windows (e.g., 72 hours), affirmative assistance with data-subject inquiries, or remediation at one party's expense -- out-of-scope for an NDA; strike or scope-limit and make mutual.
A clause purporting to license or permit secondary use of the individual's personal data (e.g., for marketing, profiling, or AI training) beyond the Purpose.
Perpetual / unlimited-in-time retention of the individual's personal data with no return/destruction obligation.
An overbroad consent purporting to authorize Amperesand (or the counterparty) to share the individual's personal data with unspecified third parties.
acceptable_fallbacks: A mutual, reasonably-scoped acknowledgment that each party will handle the other's shared personal data confidentially and use it solely for the Purpose is acceptable.

Where the individual is a California resident and Amperesand processes their personal data, a brief CCPA-consistent acknowledgment (purpose-limited use, no sale, deletion on request) is acceptable -- subject to counsel confirmation.
Returning/destroying the individual's personal data together with other CI per the return/destruction clause is the standard mechanism.

positions.title: Notices and Miscellaneous (Boilerplate)
positions.standard_position: Notices effective on delivery by hand, email, or certified/registered mail to specified addresses (template Clause 9). Clean boilerplate: no-waiver (Clause 11), severability (Clause 13), entire agreement/merger with written-signed amendments (Clause 14), counterparts with PDF/e-signature execution (Clause 17). E-signature statutory reference matched to governing law -- ESIGN + Delaware UETA on US/Delaware paper. No extra regulatory obligations. The individual's notice details (name, street address, city/state/zip, country, email) must be completed before signature -- the template leaves these as placeholders.
walk_away_triggers: Bundled Singapore-law statutory references embedded in this Delaware/US-governed agreement, creating governing-law conflict over personal-data, related-corporation, and signature-validity definitions -- must be cleaned before signing (the canonical template carries Singapore artifacts).
Attorneys'-fee / prevailing-party fee-shifting clause not in Amperesand's standard, creating asymmetric litigation cost exposure -- resist or strike (especially coercive against an individual).

Incomplete or blank counterparty notice details (placeholder name/address/email) left in an executed agreement, undermining valid service of notices -- never sign with placeholder notice fields (the template ships with these placeholders for the individual).
Securities-trading / material-non-public-information acknowledgment imposing affirmative internal compliance obligations beyond an NDA's scope -- push back as out-of-scope.
Jury-trial waiver or other US-litigation-specific boilerplate inserted where it signals counterparty drafting control toward litigation.
Perpetual / unlimited-in-time survival of personal-data or other miscellaneous obligations -- cap to a defined term.
acceptable_fallbacks: An ESIGN/UETA e-signature acknowledgment is acceptable and matches the template's PDF/e-signature counterparts clause.
A no-third-party-beneficiaries clause is acceptable and consistent with the template.
Email notice to the individual's specified personal email address is acceptable and practical.

positions.title: Entire Agreement / Amendments
positions.standard_position: The Agreement is the final, complete, and exclusive agreement of the Parties on the subject matter, superseding and merging all prior discussions; no modification or amendment is effective unless in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. (Template Clause 14.)
walk_away_triggers: Entire-agreement clause drafted to supersede or override a more protective definitive employment/consulting agreement between the Parties.
Amendment permitted by conduct, email, or one-sided written notice rather than a signed writing by both Parties.
Merger clause paired with a non-reliance provision that disclaims the AS-IS no-warranty allocation in a way disadvantaging Amperesand.
acceptable_fallbacks: A standard mutual entire-agreement + written-signed-amendment clause is acceptable and mirrors the template.
